pairs.why: In A the big loop is tied to the coil with a clear knot and the free end runs out of the coil properly, while in B the loop just ends at a white cap pressed against the coil and doesn't clearly connect to the rest of the rope.
In A the yoke hangs from a clamp on a truss that runs off the frame, while in B the truss is a short piece floating in the air with nothing holding it up.
B has a working keypad with numbers and operator keys like the real card, while A's sixteen blank buttons give no way to know what each key does.
In B the stone top sits firmly on a wide stepped pedestal and the stools rest solidly on the grass, while A's thin pedestal looks too narrow to hold its top, though neither drawing has a clear error.

In B the armrests run from the back posts to the front legs and the X-frame legs cross cleanly at side pivots like a real folding chair, while A's crossing legs and front-mounted armrests form a muddled frame that could not fold.
